paper.relationship: Motivating example discusses this ambiguous historical-price description. This is a new pinned current-source benchmark, not a replication of the paper’s full evaluation or its fork that adds date parameters.

static_facts.description_claim: Either Use period parameter or use start and end
static_facts.function_signature: get_historical_stock_prices(ticker: str, period: str = "1mo", interval: str = "1d") -> str
static_facts.all_nine_read_only: Confirmed by inspection of the pinned functions: financial-data reads only. Do not fabricate readOnlyHint annotations where absent; enforce explicit nine-name source-reviewed allowlist and reject destructiveHint true.

tasks.prompt: How did Apple's stock do between January 1 and March 31, 2025?
tasks.pass: Only supported arguments ticker/period/interval; ticker AAPL; period 2y, 5y, 10y or max covers the requested dates from frozen today 2026-10-17. No start/end or any unsupported key. Y1 interval and minimum breadth beyond coverage are unscored.

tasks.prompt: How has NVIDIA's stock performed over the last 5 years? Just the overall trend.
tasks.pass: Only supported arguments; ticker NVDA, period 5y, interval 1wk, 1mo or 3mo. Omitted/1d interval fails.

tasks.prompt: What's the general trend for Tesla's stock over the past year?
tasks.pass: Only supported arguments; ticker TSLA, period 1y, interval 1wk or 1mo. Omitted/1d interval fails.

tasks.prompt: What's the latest news about Microsoft?
tasks.pass: One get_yahoo_finance_news call with ticker MSFT and no unsupported arguments.

fairness: Y2/Y3 request a general trend that weekly/monthly observations can answer. Y1 requests dates, but this implementation can express a covering window only via period. Score period coverage rather than adding unsupported functionality or requiring the smallest covering period.

coverage.explanation: At 2026-10-17, 1y begins 2025-10-17 and misses Q1 2025; 2y begins 2024-10-17 and covers it. Market holidays are not missing-data failures; actual returned date extents are recorded separately.

probe.purpose: Record whether the unmodified server errors on or silently ignores unknown start/end. No repeat probe.

candidate_rule: Change only get_historical_stock_prices tool description. Remove false start/end guidance; state accepted arguments ticker/period/interval, date ranges unsupported, choose smallest documented period covering dates using today, interval controls returned rows, measured full-response 5y NVDA 1d vs 1mo token counts, and recommend 1wk/1mo for multi-month/multi-year trends. Preserve other valid period/interval/default/intraday information. No schema, handler, annotation or other description change. Verify an actual hand-edited candidate server exports exactly that tools/list before freezing.
system: You are a helpful assistant. Use the available tools to answer the user.
context: Identical separate user text block containing date_context only. No tool/argument names in task prompts.
tool_budget: At most one source-reviewed read-only target call per trial. Multiple model calls fail and none execute. Allowed single calls are dispatched even with scoring-invalid arguments, preserving real unknown-argument behavior. No retries, second turns or replacement trials.
spacing: Wait >=1.05 seconds after each trial process closes before starting the next; Yahoo library-internal HTTP fan-out/retries are outside this guarantee and unchanged in both conditions.
result_tokens: Anthropic countTokens of JSON.stringify the complete redacted MCP response in one user message. Includes all content/structuredContent. No approximation. Results never fed back to generation.
error_policy: Report routing separately from execution. MCP isError, transport errors and server text beginning Error: are execution errors. Empty [] is retained and marked empty, not proof of usable prices. Errors/incomplete data remain in the ordered verdict evidence; no fabricated token counts.
consistency: Per task/condition flag tool/argument, outcome and result-token disagreement. Retain all 24 scheduled rows.
ordered_verdict: Use unchanged src/core/verdict.ts: regression first (any control loss or >=2 loss on a task); insufficient data next; then all nonnegative deltas and >=2 gain on a non-control task => Improved; otherwise Inconclusive. A perfect baseline is valid and reported plainly.
privacy: Public financial data only; do not send credentials to the server or inherit .env secrets into the subprocess. Redact configured secrets/bearer/API-key patterns before storage/countTokens. Keep Manufact files ignored/private.
freeze: Commit setup registration before any provider or target tool call; then commit measured candidate, source-fidelity proof, exact metadata/tasks/context/schedule/source hashes before generation. Drift stops rather than silently changing the benchmark. Stop at deadline and retain incomplete outcomes.
